items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I succeeded Paul Hindemith, who was one of the greatest composers of the twentieth century, as a teacher there.

ctx.x: Did it surprise you to think that they knew who you were, they were monitoring you, they knew your history?

Oh yeah. I just said before – I don’t want to say it, because it sounds arrogant. I was so famous and I was so successful in so many areas of music that I was one of the most famous and most performed composers, and I was a major conductor, conducting hundreds of orchestras all over the world. I’m now a little bit forgotten, to some extent, because the young people come up, very talented people, and they take the place of the elder citizens. I say sort of forgotten. I’m not saying – but no, in those days – but…
